questions.question: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No lotus is a daisy. All lotuses are tulips. All tulips are sunflowers. Conclusions: I. All daisies are tulips. II. Some sunflowers are daisies. III. No sunflower is a daisy.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:
No lotus is a daisy.
All lotuses are tulips.
All tulips are sunflowers.

Conclusions:
I. All daisies are tulips.
II. Some sunflowers are daisies.
III. No sunflower is a daisy.

options.text: Either conclusion II or III follows
options.html: Either conclusion II or III follows

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. All daisies are tulips → Does not follow(As no lotus is a daisy and all lotuses are tulips. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. Some sunflowers are daisies → Does not follow (As no lotus is a daisy, all lotuses are tulips and all tulips are sunflowers. So it is possible but not definite.)

III. No sunflower is a daisy → Does not follow (As no lotus is a daisy, all lotuses are tulips and all tulips are sunflowers. As no direct relation is given between sunflower and daisy, so it is possible but not definite.)

questions.question: Which of the following interchanges of numbers (not digits) would make the given equation correct? \(2^{(57 - 33 \div 11 \times 13 - 2)} + 3^{(64 - 56 \div 8 \times 4 - 44)} = 35 \)
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following interchanges of numbers (not digits) would make the given equation correct?

\(2^{(57 - 33 \div 11 \times 13 - 2)} + 3^{(64 - 56 \div 8 \times 4 - 44)} = 35 \)
questions.solution:
Option  4): 33 and 44

257 - 33 ÷ 11 × 13 - 2 + 364 - 56 ÷ 8 × 4 - 44​ = 35 ⇒ 257 - 44 ÷ 11 × 13 - 2 + 364 - 56 ÷ 8 × 4 - 33​ = 35

⇒ 257 - 44 ÷ 11 × 13 - 2 + 364 - 56 ÷ 8 × 4 - 33​ = 35 ⇒ 257 - 4 × 13 - 2 + 364 - 7 × 4 - 33​ = 35 ⇒ 257 - 52 - 2 + 364 - 28 - 33​ = 35 ⇒ 23 + 33​ = 35 ⇒ 8 + 27​ = 35 ⇒ 35 = 35 (LHS = RHS)

questions.question: All of the letters in the word ‘FROWNED’ are arranged in alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is fourth from the left end and the one which is second from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.questionHtml:
All of the letters in the word ‘FROWNED’ are arranged in alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English
alphabetical series between the letter which is fourth from the left end and the one which is second from the right end in the
new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.solution:
Given word F R O W N E D
Arranged in alphabetical order D E F N O R W

Now, the number of letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the fourth from the left end and the one which is second from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed:

(Left end) D E F N O R W (Right end)

Here, three letters i.e. O, P, and Q are between N and R.

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the father of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, how is K related to O if ‘K ÷ L − M + N × O’?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’;
‘A – B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’;
‘A × B’ means ‘A is the father of B’ and
‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’.
Based on the above, how is K related to O if ‘K ÷ L − M + N × O’?
questions.solution: Thus, K is O's father’s sister or paternal aunt.

questions.question: Two different positions of the same dice are given below. Which is the number on the face opposite to the face containing 5?
questions.questionHtml: Two different positions of the same dice are given below. Which is the number on the face opposite to the face containing 5?
questions.solution:
As 3 is common on both the dices, it is clear that 1, 6, 4, and 2 are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. 5 will be opposite to it.

​

Opposite pairs:

6 → 2, 1 → 4, 3 → 5
